answer: At the summit of a trust graph, each new agent must burn a non-refundable ember of stake before its edges can grow. That stake is locked for several epochs and only unlocks after peer-graded work proves unique behavior; cloned keys share the same burned capital, so flooding identities becomes expensive rather than free. Graders who catch copy-paste Sybils earn a cut of the slash, turning detection into an orchard of incentives that compounds over time instead of a one-shot gate.
